meta.blurb: Elise misses her stop because her mind is already in tomorrow. Behind a green gate she finds Yusuf, an old gardener who draws three circles in the soil, for past, future and here. By autumn, she knows the way into the third.
meta.bible: Elise Marlow: a thirty-five-year-old hospital Scheduler who plans nurses' shifts; capable, always busy, always thinking about the next thing. Yusuf: a retired gardener of seventy-two who looks after the Garden behind a green gate near her street; unhurried, funny and kind. Aylin: Yusuf's wife, who died some years ago. Nora: Elise's older sister. Marcus: a colleague at the hospital. Lily: Nora's six-year-old daughter, Elise's niece. The Garden has beds of Beans, Carrots, Seedlings, a shed, a bench and a water barrel. Key terms: Attention, Present, Breath, Grounding, Senses, Tangerine, Trowel, Kettle, Snail, Intention, Mindfulness. The book runs through one season, from Spring to Autumn and a little beyond. Real research, mentioned carefully: a large study that asked people at random moments found that minds wandered nearly half the time, and that people tended to report feeling less happy when they were wandering; some studies suggest that naming a feeling can ease it, that time among plants and trees can help people feel calmer, and that noting a few good things each day can lift mood a little; slow breathing often helps the body settle. No other studies or numbers are invented. The book gives general practical ideas, not treatment, and says that heavy or lasting worry or low mood is a reason to talk to a doctor or counsellor. This is original practical self-help for adults, one idea in each beat, building to a final takeaway. Voice and tone: calm, concrete, warm, sometimes funny, never preachy. Priya Nair: a night nurse at the hospital, tired and kind, who later comes to the Garden. Rosa: a sixteen-year-old volunteer at the Garden who wears headphones and asks sharp questions. Tomas: Nora's husband. Biscuit: a neighbour's puppy that runs about the Garden. The Garden also has an apple tree, a small pond beneath it, a brass plaque on the bench that reads For Aylin, and a straw hat that Yusuf wears. Yusuf worked for the city parks for fifty years before he retired. Elise travels to work by Train and walks the last part along a street of cherry Blossom, past the green gate. Aylin and Yusuf were married for forty-one years and built the bench together. At twenty-two Elise turned down a place on a painting course, a regret she lets go in the Garden, and she begins to sketch again. Elise's hospital manager and a senior manager appear without names. Priya sees her doctor after Elise shares a leaflet; the book gives no diagnosis. Yusuf gives Elise his old Trowel before the first frost, and the book ends at sunrise on the garden bench in October. Twenty chapters of ten beats follow the season: each teaches one practice or idea.

beats.scene: Elise stares at her phone on a train as her stop passes
beats.summary: Elise, always thinking of the next thing, misses her train stop and cannot remember the journey.

beats.scene: Elise paces an empty platform at a small station, checking a timetable
beats.summary: Stranded at a far station, Elise waits for a train back and does sums with the minutes she is losing.

beats.scene: Elise hurries along a street of pink blossom with her eyes on her phone
beats.summary: Back at her own station, Elise rushes to work through a spring street without seeing any of it.

beats.scene: A green gate stands open in a long brick wall beside the pavement
beats.summary: Halfway along the street, Elise finds the green gate she has passed a thousand times standing open.

beats.scene: An old man in a straw hat kneels beside a bed of seedlings
beats.summary: Inside the gate, an old man looks up from his planting and asks whether she is lost.

beats.scene: Yusuf hands Elise a trowel beside a row of seedlings
beats.summary: Yusuf offers her a trowel and asks what she is thinking about, and it is next week's meeting.

beats.scene: Elise digs a crooked row of holes with a trowel while Yusuf watches
beats.summary: Elise digs a row while her mind drifts back to work, and it comes out crooked.

beats.scene: Yusuf points around the garden at beds, a shed, a bench and a barrel
beats.summary: Yusuf shows her the garden he has looked after since he retired.

beats.scene: Yusuf waves from the green gate as Elise hurries away
beats.summary: Late for work, Elise leaves, and Yusuf tells her the seeds will be there on Saturday.

beats.scene: Elise on the evening train looks out of the window, soil under her nails
beats.summary: On the train home Elise remembers every minute of the journey for the first time in months.

beats.scene: Elise opens the green gate on a bright Saturday morning, holding a paper bag
beats.summary: On Saturday Elise returns to the garden with pastries, feeling a little foolish and a little glad.

beats.scene: Yusuf draws three circles in the soil: past, future and here
beats.summary: The mind spends its time in three places: the past, the future, and here.

beats.scene: Elise shares ten pebbles between three circles drawn in the soil
beats.summary: Yusuf asks where she lives most days, and Elise puts nearly all her pebbles in the future.

beats.scene: Yusuf taps the smallest circle with his stick
beats.summary: The here circle is the smallest, but it is the only one where life can actually be touched.

beats.scene: Yusuf holds a worn magazine article while Elise leans over a wheelbarrow
beats.summary: A large study found minds wander nearly half the time, and wandering people tended to feel less happy.

beats.scene: Yusuf rings a small brass bell outside the shed while Elise holds a trowel
beats.summary: Elise tests herself: each time the bell rings, she says where her mind was.

beats.scene: Yusuf and Elise watch a neighbour's puppy bounding across the grass
beats.summary: A mind is like a puppy: it runs off, and you do not scold it, you call it back.

beats.scene: Yusuf taps the soil beside a circle marked here with a stick
beats.summary: The moment you notice you have wandered, you are already back, and that moment is the practice.

beats.scene: Elise sits on the bench with a worried face while Yusuf pours tea
beats.summary: Elise fears she has wasted half her life, and Yusuf says every moment from now is still hers.

beats.scene: Rain washes the three circles from the soil while they shelter in the shed
beats.summary: Rain washes the circles away, but Elise remembers them as she walks home in the damp light.

beats.scene: Elise lies awake in bed, a thought-cloud of an old argument above her
beats.summary: At night Elise replays a conversation with her sister Nora from a month ago.

beats.scene: Elise tells Yusuf about her sleepless night while they weed the beans
beats.summary: Elise tells Yusuf about the replaying, and he calls the past a film on a loop.

beats.scene: Yusuf holds a withered tomato plant and shakes his head with a smile
beats.summary: Yusuf tells how he replayed one forgotten night of frost until the tomatoes were long gone.

beats.scene: Elise walks round and round the shed while Yusuf watches from the bench
beats.summary: Replaying feels like solving a problem, but it is more like walking in circles in a small room.

beats.scene: Elise types a short message to her sister on the garden bench
beats.summary: Yusuf asks whether there is anything she can do now, and Elise sends Nora a message.

beats.scene: Elise reads her sister's warm reply on the bench, smiling with relief
beats.summary: Nora replies kindly, but Elise's mind still wants to replay the film that night.

beats.scene: Elise lies in bed with her lamp on and her hand on the blanket
beats.summary: The film starts again that night, so Elise names it and feels the blanket instead.

beats.scene: Yusuf lays a white cover over young plants on a cold evening
beats.summary: The past is useful if it teaches: Yusuf now keeps a frost cover ready in the shed.

beats.scene: Elise smiles at an old photograph of two girls holding ice creams
beats.summary: A happy memory is fine as a visit, if you do not move in: Elise remembers summers with Nora.

beats.scene: Elise steps carefully into the smallest circle drawn in fresh soil
beats.summary: Yusuf redraws the circles, and Elise steps into the smallest one and stands there.

beats.scene: Elise frowns at a desk calendar full of meeting boxes
beats.summary: Worry is the mind rehearsing a future that may never happen.

beats.scene: Yusuf rakes a bed of soil while Elise sits on an upturned bucket
beats.summary: Yusuf calls worry a rehearsal for a play that may never open, and Elise sees her own calendar.

beats.scene: Elise ticks a list of worries in a small notebook on the garden bench
beats.summary: Elise keeps a list for a week of what she worries about and what actually happens.

beats.scene: Yusuf stretches a string line along the beans while Elise writes a list
beats.summary: Planning is a tool that ends in an action, but worry goes round in circles.

beats.scene: Elise writes one next step beside each item on a list headed Thursday
beats.summary: A simple test: if a worry has a next step, write it down and do it; if not, let it be.

beats.scene: Yusuf holds out an umbrella beneath a clear blue sky and grins
beats.summary: Worry does not protect us from rain; the umbrella is the plan.

beats.scene: Elise writes next week's shifts on a pad while sitting on the garden bench
beats.summary: Planning is real work: Elise plans next week's rota for fifteen minutes and finishes.

beats.scene: Elise closes her notebook and pencil case with a satisfied click
beats.summary: Planning has an ending: Elise closes the notebook and lets the rest go.

beats.scene: Elise pulls weeds from the bean bed with a thoughtful frown
beats.summary: While weeding, Elise catches her mind rehearsing a meeting and quietly names it rehearsing.

beats.scene: A bright green bean shoot pushes up through dark soil
beats.summary: The first bean shoots appear: things grow here and now, not in the worry.

beats.scene: Elise holds a warm cup of tea in both hands in the garden shed
beats.summary: Life only ever happens now, because everything we do takes place in this moment.

beats.scene: Elise and Yusuf sit at a small wooden table with a teapot
beats.summary: Elise objects that the past made her who she is, and Yusuf agrees but says it reaches her now.

beats.scene: Yusuf holds two cups, one full and one empty, with a smile
beats.summary: Yusuf proves the point playfully: you cannot drink tomorrow's tea or yesterday's.

beats.scene: Yusuf kneels in the soil and pats the ground beside him
beats.summary: Yusuf invites Elise to begin: close your eyes and press your hands into the soil.

beats.scene: Elise presses her hands into dark soil with her eyes closed
beats.summary: A first practice: feel the soil with your hands and notice sensations.

beats.scene: Elise holds her hands still in the soil and feels a warm patch beneath
beats.summary: Deeper down the soil is warmer, and a worm moves, and Elise jumps and then laughs.

beats.scene: Elise sits very still with her eyes closed and a gentle expression
beats.summary: For a few seconds the thoughts go quiet, the first rest her mind has had for weeks.

beats.scene: Elise holds up a muddy hand and frowns slightly at her own thoughts
beats.summary: A thought arrives, did I lock the car, and Yusuf says it is fine, just come back to the hands.

beats.scene: Elise rinses her muddy hands in the cold water of the rain barrel
beats.summary: Elise washes her hands in the barrel and feels the water: the practice is simply feeling what is here.

beats.scene: Yusuf points to a steaming cup of tea on the bench as Elise leaves
beats.summary: To make it last, Yusuf suggests a small habit: one chosen moment each day to feel what is here.

beats.scene: Yusuf holds up five fingers in front of Elise in the sunny garden
beats.summary: Yusuf teaches a quick trick for noisy moments: name five things you see, four you feel, and so on.

beats.scene: Elise looks around the garden pointing at a bucket, a robin and a ladder
beats.summary: Elise names five things she can see: a blue bucket, a robin, a ladder, a snail and a patch of sun.

beats.scene: Elise touches a warm bench, rough bark and a cool metal trowel
beats.summary: Elise names four things she can touch: the warm bench, rough bark, a cool trowel and her soft sleeve.

beats.scene: Elise sits with her eyes closed and a hand cupped to her ear
beats.summary: Elise names three things she can hear: a sparrow, a far bus and the wind in the beans.

beats.scene: Elise sniffs a tomato leaf and sips a hot mug of mint tea
beats.summary: Two smells and one taste: tomato leaves, damp earth and sweet mint tea.

beats.scene: Elise stands with her feet flat on the grass and her eyes open wide
beats.summary: Why it works: the senses are always in the present, so they are a door back to now.

beats.scene: Rosa in headphones leans on a watering can and looks sceptical
beats.summary: Rosa, a teenage volunteer, asks if this is only paying attention, and Yusuf says yes, that is all of it.

beats.scene: Elise stands on a crowded platform quietly counting what she can see
beats.summary: On Monday morning Elise uses the trick on a crowded platform while a train rattles in.

beats.scene: Elise stands with her feet flat on a hospital corridor floor
beats.summary: In a hospital corridor, after a tense phone call, Elise steadies herself by naming what is around her.

beats.scene: Elise sits at her desk with a small smile, a hand on her notebook
beats.summary: The practice does not remove stress, but it gives Elise somewhere steady to stand.

beats.scene: Elise sits on a bench with her eyes closed and Yusuf beside her
beats.summary: The breath is always with you and always in the present, so it is a place to return to.

beats.scene: Elise breathes slowly with one hand resting on her stomach
beats.summary: Three slow breaths, counted: they take longer than Elise imagined.

beats.scene: Elise lowers her shoulders on the bench and lets her jaw relax
beats.summary: Slow breathing often helps the body settle, and Elise's shoulders come down from her ears.

beats.scene: Elise opens one eye and looks at Yusuf with a rueful grin
beats.summary: Elise loses count at breath two; Yusuf says to start again at one, because there are no prizes.

beats.scene: Elise lies on the grass watching white clouds drift across a blue sky
beats.summary: Thoughts are like weather passing through the sky; they are not facts.

beats.scene: Elise holds a pencil over a page that reads I will never finish
beats.summary: Elise writes down a gloomy thought, I will never finish, and sees that it is only a cloud.

beats.scene: Elise glares at a dark storm cloud gathering above the garden
beats.summary: A big dark thought, I am no good at this, arrives, and Yusuf calls it a storm that will pass.

beats.scene: Elise sits with her eyes closed, a small smile, and clouds drifting above
beats.summary: Elise silently labels thoughts as planning or remembering, like naming clouds, and they lose their pull.

beats.scene: Elise looks up through the apple branches at a patch of clear sky
beats.summary: Behind every cloud the sky is still there, and Elise glimpses the part of her that simply watches.

beats.scene: Elise waits at a pedestrian crossing, breathing slowly, a hand on her bag strap
beats.summary: Yusuf gives homework: three slow breaths at every crossing, and Elise finds many small doors in her day.

beats.scene: Elise sits at her office desk, eyes shut, a screen of schedules glowing
beats.summary: At work, Elise tries to stay calm for a minute and fails, but Yusuf says wandering is normal.

beats.scene: Elise opens her eyes at her desk as a telephone rings beside her
beats.summary: Thoughts rush in, a phone rings, and Elise gives up after forty seconds.

beats.scene: Elise shakes her head sadly on the garden bench while Yusuf listens
beats.summary: On Saturday Elise reports her failure, and Yusuf says wandering is normal and noticing is the point.

beats.scene: Yusuf lifts a heavy watering can with a smile while Elise watches
beats.summary: Each time you notice and return, you strengthen your attention, like a repetition at the gym.

beats.scene: Elise counts on her fingers beside a row of watering cans
beats.summary: Elise counts seventeen returns in three minutes, and Yusuf cheers each one like a gym coach.

beats.scene: Yusuf rests on a spade, shaking his head and laughing at himself
beats.summary: Yusuf admits that he still wanders, once digging the wrong bed while thinking about lunch.

beats.scene: Elise talks to Priya, a night nurse, beside a drinks machine
beats.summary: Priya, a tired night nurse, notices that Elise seems calmer and asks her secret.

beats.scene: Elise and Priya sit on plastic chairs in a quiet staff room corner
beats.summary: Priya says she cannot switch off after her night shifts, and she says she could use a garden.

beats.scene: Elise sits at her desk with both feet flat on the floor
beats.summary: Elise builds a cue into her day: every time she sits down, she feels her feet on the floor.

beats.scene: Elise holds up a small radish with soil on it, grinning widely
beats.summary: The first radishes are ready, and Elise pulls one herself, proud of something she waited for.

beats.scene: Elise kneels at a seed bed marked with a small wooden sign
beats.summary: Carrots cannot be hurried; patience is part of the practice.

beats.scene: Elise reaches towards a seedling and Yusuf catches her hand
beats.summary: Elise wants to dig up a seed to check it, and Yusuf stops her: pulling does not speed it up.

beats.scene: Elise reads an urgent staff email while tapping a pencil on her desk
beats.summary: At work, Elise wants a staffing problem solved in a day, but it depends on replies that cannot be rushed.

beats.scene: Elise sits in the garden shed with a cup of tea and a list
beats.summary: Do your part, then let the soil do its part: Elise learns to wait without worrying.

beats.scene: Elise chops vegetables slowly on a wooden board with her phone out of sight
beats.summary: Doing one thing at a time: cooking dinner with full attention.

beats.scene: Elise wipes her eyes while peeling an onion, smiling through tears
beats.summary: Onion, knife, steam and sizzle: Elise notices what cooking is really like.

beats.scene: Elise stirs a pot of tomato sauce and tastes it from a wooden spoon
beats.summary: While the sauce simmers, Elise's mind drifts to email, she returns, and for once she tastes the garlic.

beats.scene: Elise eats at a small table beside a dark, switched-off television
beats.summary: Elise eats at the table with the television off, slowly, tasting each mouthful.

beats.scene: Elise looks at two spinning plates drawn on a sticky note
beats.summary: Yusuf says that doing two things at once usually means doing each a little worse.

beats.scene: A cluster of feathery green carrot seedlings pokes up from the soil
beats.summary: The first carrot seedlings appear at last, and Elise kneels to look at them, delighted.

beats.scene: Elise sits on her sofa beside a sticky note covered in tally marks
beats.summary: Elise counts how many times she picks up her phone in one evening, and the number shocks her.

beats.scene: Elise's phone lights up with a message while a book lies open
beats.summary: The phone breaks attention into pieces: every ping pulls her away from what she is doing.

beats.scene: Elise places her phone face down in a drawer at the dinner table
beats.summary: The phone breaks attention into pieces, so Elise puts it away at meals.

beats.scene: Elise eats toast at the kitchen table, listening to the quiet and the clock
beats.summary: After a week the quiet fills with noticing: the clock, the toast, the light on the table.

beats.scene: Elise rings a doorbell, holding a bunch of flowers and a gift bag
beats.summary: Elise goes to Sunday lunch at Nora's house, with her phone left in her coat pocket.

beats.scene: Elise and Nora sit across a kitchen table while Tomas washes dishes behind them
beats.summary: Elise apologises about the cancelled dinner, and Nora says she has been tired and worried too.

beats.scene: Elise leans forward and listens, with her hands in her lap
beats.summary: Real listening: Elise gives her sister her whole attention for the first time in a long while.

beats.scene: Nora wipes her eyes with a napkin while Elise holds her hand
beats.summary: Nora cries a little and says that Elise is really here for once, which stings and warms her at once.

beats.scene: Lily holds up a drawing of a purple dragon while Elise kneels to look
beats.summary: Lily shows Elise a drawing of a purple dragon, and Elise really looks, and Lily glows.

beats.scene: Elise walks home at dusk in summer light, holding a rolled-up drawing
beats.summary: Elise walks home with the dragon drawing and realises it was the best Sunday she has had in a year.

beats.scene: Elise peels a tangerine and looks closely at one segment
beats.summary: Eating slowly: one tangerine segment, tasted with full attention.

beats.scene: Elise holds one glistening tangerine segment up to the sunlight
beats.summary: Elise studies a single segment: the fine white threads, the glistening skin, the tiny bubbles of juice.

beats.scene: Elise closes her eyes and slowly chews a piece of tangerine
beats.summary: She tastes it slowly: sweet first, then sharp, and one segment lasts a full minute.

beats.scene: Elise sits at her kitchen counter with toast and tea by the window
beats.summary: On workdays Elise picks one meal to eat slowly, and her breakfast becomes the best part of her morning.

beats.scene: Elise and Yusuf walk slowly along a gravel path between the beds
beats.summary: Walking: feel your feet, notice the air, and arrive.

beats.scene: Elise walks to work under a canopy of leaves, looking up at the trees
beats.summary: On the way to work Elise feels her feet and notices the leaves, and she arrives instead of just reaching the door.

beats.scene: Elise glances at her watch while walking at a calm, even pace
beats.summary: Elise always walks as if she is late, so she tries a slower pace and arrives only two minutes later.

beats.scene: Elise stands in a slow shop queue with a basket on her arm
beats.summary: Waiting is a free chance to practise, instead of a loss of time.

beats.scene: Elise breathes calmly in a queue behind an old man with soup
beats.summary: Elise breathes, feels her feet, and notices the people in the queue as people.

beats.scene: Elise smiles in a slow queue, sunlight falling through the shop window
beats.summary: Every queue becomes a free bench: Elise decides that waiting is not lost time.

beats.scene: Elise writes the word nervous on a sticky note
beats.summary: Putting a name to a feeling can ease it.

beats.scene: Elise holds the sticky note and speaks the word aloud in a quiet corridor
beats.summary: Elise says I notice I feel nervous, and Yusuf later explains that naming a feeling can ease it.

beats.scene: Elise writes three words on a sticky note: nervous, tired, hopeful
beats.summary: Elise finds more exact words for what she feels: nervous, tired and a little hopeful.

beats.scene: Elise rests a hand on her chest in a quiet room
beats.summary: Feelings live in the body: notice where the worry sits, and breathe toward it.

beats.scene: Elise places a hand on her stomach with her eyes closed
beats.summary: Elise finds a tightness behind her breastbone and a knot in her stomach, and she describes its shape.

beats.scene: Elise breathes out slowly with a hand resting over her stomach
beats.summary: Breathing toward the knot, Elise feels it loosen a little, though it does not disappear.

beats.scene: Yusuf points at a puddle in the garden as raindrops make ripples that settle
beats.summary: Yusuf says feelings are weather in the body: they rise, peak and fall if you let them.

beats.scene: Elise talks quietly with Yusuf on the bench while the afternoon light turns golden
beats.summary: Elise tells Yusuf she is afraid of Friday's review, and he does not fix it; he just listens.

beats.scene: Elise sits straight in a hospital meeting room, hands folded on the table
beats.summary: On Friday Elise feels nervous in the review, names it, breathes, and speaks honestly.

beats.scene: Elise leaves a meeting room, a hand on her chest, smiling quietly
beats.summary: The review goes well enough, and Elise leaves feeling that she stayed herself.

beats.scene: Yusuf pushes a beach ball under water in a barrel
beats.summary: Pushing feelings away takes effort and does not last, like holding a ball under water.

beats.scene: Yusuf lets go of the ball, and it springs up with a splash
beats.summary: When Yusuf lets go, the ball shoots up and drenches him, and Elise sees her own pushed-down feelings.

beats.scene: Elise sits quietly on the bench with one hand on her heart
beats.summary: Elise lets a sadness she has pushed away float beside her, and it rises, peaks and fades.

beats.scene: Elise reads a sharp email on her screen with her jaw clenched
beats.summary: An angry email arrives from a senior manager, and Elise feels heat rush into her face.

beats.scene: Elise breathes, one hand flat on the desk, an angry email on screen
beats.summary: When angry, pause for three breaths before replying.

beats.scene: Elise types a short calm reply and the sender's friendly answer appears
beats.summary: Elise writes a calm two-line reply, and the manager answers politely and thanks her.

beats.scene: Yusuf shows Elise a nettle with a leaf in his gloved hand
beats.summary: Yusuf says that anger is information and not an order: it tells you that something matters.

beats.scene: Elise writes on a crumpled old note beside a cup of tea
beats.summary: Regret: Elise writes down the thing she regrets, that she never took the painting course.

beats.scene: Elise folds a paper boat on the garden bench while Yusuf looks on
beats.summary: Take the lesson, then let the past go: Elise folds her regret into a paper boat.

beats.scene: Elise sketches the green gate with a pencil on the back of an envelope
beats.summary: The boat floats away on the pond, and Elise sketches the green gate with a pencil.

beats.scene: Elise drops a tray in the hospital canteen, muttering angrily at herself
beats.summary: Elise drops a tray and calls herself stupid, and Yusuf later asks what she would say to Nora.

beats.scene: Elise speaks gently to her own reflection in a bathroom mirror
beats.summary: Treat yourself as you would treat a good friend.

beats.scene: Elise looks at herself in a mirror and smiles gently
beats.summary: She tells herself that she is doing her best, which feels awkward but true.

beats.scene: Yusuf shouts at a row of seedlings with a comic frown, then laughs
beats.summary: Kindness is not laziness: Yusuf never shouted at a seedling and made it grow faster.

beats.scene: Elise lies awake in bed with a notebook and lamp on the bedside table
beats.summary: Sleep: write down tomorrow's worries earlier, and use the breath or body when thoughts race at night.

beats.scene: Elise writes a short list at a desk lamp before bed
beats.summary: Elise writes tomorrow's worries in a notebook early in the evening, so that they are not waiting at night.

beats.scene: Elise lies under a blanket with her hand on her stomach, eyes closed
beats.summary: At three in the morning, Elise feels the blanket and her feet, and the racing thoughts slow, though not perfectly.

beats.scene: Elise rests quietly in bed with her eyes open and a small lamp glowing
beats.summary: If sleep will not come, Elise lets herself rest anyway, and she stops fighting the night.

beats.scene: Elise frowns at Marcus in a hospital corridor, holding a form
beats.summary: A bad day: Elise snaps at a colleague, Marcus, over a missing form, and she sees his face fall.

beats.scene: Elise apologises to her colleague Marcus in a hospital corridor
beats.summary: Elise apologises at once, and she simply begins again; every moment is a fresh start.

beats.scene: Elise takes a slow breath before opening her email at a bright desk
beats.summary: At work: one breath before each task helps Elise start calmly.

beats.scene: Elise pauses at a hospital ward door with her hand on the handle
beats.summary: The one breath becomes a doorway: before each new room, Elise stops for a moment and arrives.

beats.scene: Elise frowns over a winter staffing chart spread across her desk
beats.summary: A real worry appears: winter staffing may fall short, and Elise cannot stop thinking about it.

beats.scene: Yusuf sits on a bucket with a mug of tea and an alarm clock
beats.summary: Worry time: Yusuf tells Elise to set aside ten minutes a day to worry on purpose.

beats.scene: Elise sits with a timer and a list headed worries and next steps
beats.summary: Worry time: ten minutes to list worries and the next step for each, then let go.

beats.scene: Elise whispers to herself in a supermarket aisle, holding a basket
beats.summary: When a worry pops up at other times, Elise tells it to come back at half past six.

beats.scene: Elise writes nothing to do now beside a worry on her paper
beats.summary: Some worries have no next step, so Elise writes nothing to do now, and finds it restful.

beats.scene: Elise crosses off finished items on a long list at her kitchen table
beats.summary: After a week the list shrinks: some worries were solved, and some quietly expired.

beats.scene: Priya in her nurse's uniform stands at the green gate looking nervous
beats.summary: Priya comes to the garden for the first time after a night shift, curious and tired.

beats.scene: Elise watches Priya press her hands into the soil with her eyes closed
beats.summary: Priya's first minute in the soil: her shoulders drop, and Elise sees the garden through new eyes.

beats.scene: Light from a window falls on a wall as Elise watches it

B1B2: Elise Marlow plans shifts for hospital nurses, and her mind is always on the next thing. One morning she misses her stop, and she cannot remember a single minute of the journey.
The station is small and empty, and the train back is not due for twenty minutes. Elise sends an apologetic message to the office and paces up and down the platform.
Back at her own station at last, Elise hurries towards the hospital along a street of pink blossom. She does not look up once, because she is busy rebuilding the week's shifts in her head.
Halfway along the street, a green gate stands open in an old brick wall. Elise has passed it a thousand times, but today she hears birds singing behind it.
An old man in a straw hat is kneeling beside a bed of small plants. He looks up, smiles, and asks whether she is lost.
Yusuf, who is seventy-two, hands her a trowel and says she can help him if she likes. He asks what she is thinking about, and she admits that she is planning next week's meeting.
Elise digs a row of small holes while her mind drifts back to the hospital. When she looks down, the row curves like a river, and Yusuf only laughs kindly.

Yusuf explains that the garden belongs to the whole neighbourhood, and that he has looked after it since he retired. There are beds of beans and carrots, a wooden shed, a bench, and a big barrel of rainwater.
Elise looks at her watch and gasps, because she is now very late for work. Yusuf walks her to the gate and says that the seeds will be there on Saturday.
That evening, on the train home, Elise puts her phone in her bag and looks out of the window. There is still soil under her fingernails, and for once she remembers the whole journey.
On Saturday morning, Elise is back at the green gate with a bag of warm pastries. She feels slightly silly, but Yusuf greets her as if they have known each other for years.
Yusuf draws three circles in the soil with a stick. He explains that the mind can be in the past, in the future, or here, and that most minds are hardly ever here.
Yusuf gives her ten pebbles and asks her to share them out as her week usually goes. Elise puts six in the future, three in the past, and only one in here.
Yusuf taps the smallest circle with his stick and says that it is small because it holds only this moment. It is also the only circle where she can actually do anything.

Yusuf shows her an article about a large study that asked people at random moments what they were thinking. It found that minds wandered nearly half the time, and that wandering people tended to feel less happy.
Yusuf proposes a game: every few minutes he will ring a small bell, and Elise must say where her mind was. The first three rings find her in the future, then in the past, then in the future again.
A neighbour's puppy called Biscuit races across the grass with a stolen glove. Yusuf says that a mind is exactly like this, because it runs off, and you do not scold it but simply call it back.
Yusuf tells her that she cannot stop her mind from leaving. But the moment she notices that it has gone, she is already back, and that moment is the whole practice.
Elise worries that she has spent half her life somewhere else in her head. Yusuf says that no one has wasted anything, because the next moment is always still available.
Rain begins to fall, and the three circles slowly disappear from the soil. Elise and Yusuf shelter in the shed, drink their tea, and listen to the drops on the roof.
At night, Elise lies awake and replays a conversation with her sister Nora. A month ago she cancelled Lily's birthday dinner at the last minute, and she still hears her own sharp voice.
Elise admits that she often lies awake and replays old conversations. Yusuf says that the past is a film on a loop, and the mind keeps watching it although nothing can change.
Yusuf tells her about his first summer in the garden, when a late frost killed every tomato plant. He had forgotten to cover them, and he replayed that evening for a whole year.
Yusuf says that replaying feels like thinking, but it is really walking in circles in a small room. Elise walks around the shed three times, and ends up exactly where she began.
Yusuf suggests a question: is there something she can actually do now about this? Elise thinks, then types a short message to Nora to say that she is sorry about the dinner.
Nora replies within the hour, and her message is warm and short. She says thank you, and that Lily would love to see her soon.
That night the old film starts again, even though she has already apologised. This time Elise whispers that it is only the film, and she feels the weight of the blanket and the pillow under her head.
Yusuf lays a white cover over the young plants because the night will be cold. He says the past is not for living in, but for learning from, and the tomatoes taught him this.
Elise finds an old photograph of herself and Nora eating ice creams at the seaside. She feels warm and happy, and she knows that it is good to visit the past, if she does not move in.
Yusuf draws the three circles again after the rain, and Elise steps into the smallest. Standing in it, she feels the sun on her neck and the earth firm under her shoes.
At her desk, Elise looks at a calendar crowded with meeting boxes. In her head she has already argued with most of the people in them, and she is tired before the day has begun.
Yusuf says that the future is a trap of a different kind: the mind rehearses a play that may never open. Elise thinks of her calendar and laughs, because she has rehearsed hundreds.
For one week Elise keeps a list of her worries, and each evening she writes what really happened. Most of them never came true, and the few that did were easier than she had imagined.
Elise asks whether it is wrong to make plans at all. Yusuf says no, because planning is a tool that ends in an action, while worry only goes round in circles.
Yusuf gives her a simple test for each worry. If she can take a step, she should write it down, and if there is no step, she should let the worry rest.
Elise says that worrying feels like a way to protect herself. Yusuf opens an umbrella on a sunny day and says that worry cannot change the weather, but an umbrella can help.
Elise decides to plan next week's shifts right there on the bench, with a pad and a pencil. She gives it fifteen minutes of full attention, and it is done sooner than she expected.
When the plan is finished, Elise closes the notebook. She says to herself that the planning is over, and that for now there is nothing else to do about next week.
While Elise weeds the beans, her mind begins to rehearse a conversation with her manager. She notices it, whispers the word rehearsing, and returns to the weed in her hand.
On Saturday morning, a row of bright green bean shoots has pushed up through the soil. Yusuf says that nothing in the garden grows in the future, because it grows right here, a little at a time.
Over a cup of tea in the shed, Yusuf tells Elise that everything she has ever done happened in the present moment. Everything she will ever do will happen in one as well.
Elise objects that her past made her who she is. Yusuf agrees, but he points out that she can only feel it and use it now.
Yusuf holds up two cups and says that one is yesterday's tea and the other is tomorrow's. Elise tries to drink both, and she can drink neither.
Yusuf asks her to kneel beside him, close her eyes and press her hands into the soil. He says there is nothing to achieve, only something to notice.
Elise notices that the soil is cool, damp and slightly rough. Small stones press against her fingers, and a few crumbs of earth slide between them.
Deeper in the soil, Elise finds a patch of warmth left by the morning sun. Then something wriggles against her finger, and she jumps and laughs.
For a few seconds, while she feels the soil, Elise's thoughts go quiet. It is not a miracle, but it is the first rest that her mind has had for weeks.
In the middle of the exercise a thought arrives: did she lock the car? Yusuf says that thoughts will always arrive, and that she only needs to return to her hands.
To wash her muddy hands, Elise dips them in the rain barrel. The water is cold and clear, and she feels every ripple around her wrists.
Yusuf tells her that she does not need a garden to practise. She can pick one small moment each day, and simply feel whatever is in front of her.
Yusuf teaches her a quick trick for noisy moments. She names five things she can see, four that she can touch, three that she can hear, and two that she can smell.
First Elise names five things that she can see. There is a blue bucket, a robin on the fence, a ladder against the shed, a snail, and a bright patch of sun.
Next she names four things that she can touch. The bench is warm, the apple bark is rough, the trowel is cool, and her sleeve is soft.
With her eyes closed, she listens for three sounds in the garden. A sparrow is chirping, a bus is passing far away, and the wind is moving through the bean leaves.
For smell, she picks the green scent of tomato leaves and the smell of damp earth. For taste, Yusuf gives her a mug of hot mint tea, and she drinks slowly.
Yusuf explains why the trick works so well for her. The senses always live in the present, so each time Elise uses them, she steps back through a door into the here and now.
Rosa, a sixteen-year-old volunteer, pulls off her headphones and asks whether this is only paying attention. Yusuf smiles and says yes, that is all of it, and that it is harder than it sounds.
On Monday morning, the platform is crowded and the train is late. Instead of reaching for her phone, Elise quietly names five things she can see.
After a tense phone call about a ward with too few nurses, Elise's heart is racing in the corridor. She stands still and names what she can see: a green line, a clock, a poster and a trolley.
Elise notices that the practice does not make her problems disappear at all. It does, however, give her a steady place to stand while she decides what to do.
Yusuf tells her that the breath is the most faithful companion she has. It is always with her, and it is always happening now.
Yusuf asks her to take three slow breaths and to count them carefully. She is surprised by how much longer three breaths take than she expected.
Slow breathing often helps the body to settle, and Elise feels it happen. Her shoulders come down from her ears, and her jaw loosens.
Elise loses count at the second breath and says that she has failed. Yusuf tells her to begin again at one, because there are no prizes in this.
Yusuf asks Elise to watch the clouds for a while. He says that thoughts are like weather that passes through the sky, and that they are not facts.
Elise writes down the thought that she will never finish all her work. Seeing it on paper, she realises that it is a passing cloud and not a forecast.
A heavy thought arrives, which says that she is no good at this practice. Yusuf calls it a storm cloud, and says that even storms pass.
